\section[la protesta]{la protesta — the protest}

\label{lesson:IT-C364-protesta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the freedom, then the Italian for the equality.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la protesta}
\textbf{la protesta} — \textquotedblleft{}the protest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La protesta degli studenti è durata tre giorni.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The students' protest lasted three days.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Per protesta} — as a protest.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{protesta} is built on \emph{protestare}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{prōtestārī} \textquotedblleft{}to declare in public\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{testis} \textquotedblleft{}a witness\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la protesta}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la protesta}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la protesta}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the freedom, then the Italian for the equality, then say \emph{la protesta} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la protesta mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The protest\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[protestare]{protestare — to protest}

\label{lesson:IT-C364-protestare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the equality, then the Italian for the protest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: protestare}
\textbf{protestare} — \textquotedblleft{}to protest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
I cittadini protestano contro il nuovo parcheggio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The citizens are protesting against the new car park.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Protestare contro qualcosa}. Stress: \emph{protèsto}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{protestare} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{prōtestārī} \textquotedblleft{}to declare publicly\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built from \emph{prō} \textquotedblleft{}before\textquotedblright{} and \emph{testārī} \textquotedblleft{}to bear witness\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{testis} \textquotedblleft{}a witness\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{protestare}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{protestare}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{protestare}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the equality, then the Italian for the protest, then say \emph{protestare} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does protestare mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To protest\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la manifestazione]{la manifestazione — the demonstration, the march; the event}

\label{lesson:IT-C364-manifestazione}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the protest, then the Italian for to protest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la manifestazione}
\textbf{la manifestazione} — \textquotedblleft{}the demonstration, the march; the event\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Sabato c'è una manifestazione per la pace.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{On Saturday there is a march for peace.}
\end{quote}

It can also be any public event: \emph{una manifestazione sportiva}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{manifestazione} is a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{manifestātiō} \textquotedblleft{}a making plain\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{manifestāre}, built on \emph{manifestus} \textquotedblleft{}evident, plain\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la manifestazione}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la manifestazione}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la manifestazione}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the protest, then the Italian for to protest, then say \emph{la manifestazione} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la manifestazione mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The demonstration, the march; the event\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[manifestare]{manifestare — to demonstrate; to show (a feeling)}

\label{lesson:IT-C364-manifestare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to protest, then the Italian for the demonstration.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: manifestare}
\textbf{manifestare} — \textquotedblleft{}to demonstrate; to show (a feeling)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Migliaia di persone manifestano in piazza.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Thousands of people are demonstrating in the square.}
\end{quote}

Also to show: \emph{manifestare la propria gioia}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{manifestare} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{manifestāre} \textquotedblleft{}to make plain, to show\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{manifestus} \textquotedblleft{}evident, plain\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[lo striscione]{lo striscione — the banner}

\label{lesson:IT-C364-striscione}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the demonstration, then the Italian for to demonstrate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: lo striscione}
\textbf{lo striscione} — \textquotedblleft{}the banner\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Sullo striscione c'era scritto: più scuole, meno traffico.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The banner said: more schools, less traffic.}
\end{quote}

Big and long, held by two people or hung from a balcony; also at the stadium.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{striscione} is a big \emph{striscia} \textquotedblleft{}strip, stripe\textquotedblright{}, with the ending \emph{-one} \textquotedblleft{}big\textquotedblright{}. EtymDB links \emph{striscia} to Latin \emph{stria} \textquotedblleft{}a furrow, a groove\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), but other dictionaries treat its origin as not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lo striscione}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lo striscione}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{lo striscione}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the demonstration, then the Italian for to demonstrate, then say \emph{lo striscione} again
\end{itemize}
